I added `std::cerr << "[auth] validating token\n";` immediately before each of the 4 direct call sites of `AuthToken::validate`:

- `src/web/auth_controller.cpp` — `AuthController::handleLogin` (line 13) and `AuthController::handleRefresh` (line 26)
- `src/auth/auth_service.cpp` — `AuthService::login` (line 14)
- `src/web/session_controller.cpp` — `SessionController::handle` (line 12)

Note: `ast-tool callers`/`references` reported zero results for `auth::AuthToken::validate` — it appears the resolver doesn't follow calls through reference-typed members (`AuthToken& token_`). I cross-checked with Grep and manual reading of each call site to confirm all four are genuine calls to `AuthToken::validate` on a `token_` member of that type (as opposed to `AuthService::validate`, a same-named but unrelated method that only calls `cache_.get()`). All three edited files already `#include <iostream>`, so no new includes were needed.
